name: Thermal Vision
summary: The world through an infrared camera: every surface is a temperature mapped through an ironbow ramp; warm bodies glow white-hot.
description: Nothing in this style is painted in colour. Every pixel – ground, props, creatures, particles, icons – is first a temperature between 0 and 1 and only then mapped through a single false-colour ramp: black, deep indigo, violet, magenta, crimson, orange, yellow, white. Cold ground and tree canopies sit in indigo and near-black, warm bodies glow orange with white-hot faces and cores, limbs read cooler at their rims and radiate a soft halo. A camera UI frames everything: corner brackets, a temperature scale bar, °C readouts, a blinking REC dot, a tracking box, sensor grain and heat shimmer above hot sources.
avoidFor: colour-coded puzzle games that need many hues
projects that need material colour (wood, fabric, skin tones)

difficulty.why: A new asset is just shapes filled with one temperature each – no palette decisions, the ramp guarantees consistency, and the shared heat bake adds rim cooling and halos automatically. The real work is thinking in temperature: every subject needs a hot focal point (face, core, eye), a cooler insulated or cold part for contrast, and enough temperature difference to its neighbours, otherwise two subjects merge into one orange blob.

technique.resolution: Native display resolution. Sprites baked once at 4 px per world unit; ground chunks of 256 units at up to 2.5 px/unit. The look is deliberately soft: temperature diffuses, only silhouettes and crisp ground masks stay sharp.
technique.summary: Paint temperature, not colour: shapes are filled with gray values (gray = temperature, alpha = coverage) on an offscreen canvas, a small heat pipeline (box-blur diffusion, limb cooling at the rim, a halo only around warm things) produces a temperature map, and a 256-entry LUT quantised to 72 bands maps it to the ironbow ramp. Variants (white-hot flash, cooled down, sensor afterimage) are other transfer functions on the same map.
technique.linework: No outlines. Silhouettes are defined by temperature contrast alone: every body gets a cooler rim from limb cooling (up to 42 % cooler where the 1.5-unit halo blur coverage drops below 77 %), plus a hot-only halo outside. Detail lines (fissures, quills, straps, furrows) are 0.4–1.8 unit strokes in their own temperature.
technique.shading: Temperature gradients instead of light: radial gradients from a warm core (chest, face, furnace) to cooler edges, then a 0.55-unit 3-pass box-blur diffusion mixed 50/50 into the painted values. The 72-band LUT gives faint contour banding in smooth gradients.
technique.lighting: There is no light – only emission. Hot subjects are bright, cold ones dark; warm bodies heat the ground under them (contact glow), leave fading warm footprints and breath clouds. A lens vignette cools the frame edges; strong heat events briefly brighten the whole frame (auto gain).
technique.texture: Sensor texture only: tileable fbm noise in the ground (±0.034 and ±0.017 temperature), animated grain (4 tiles of light/dark speckles with fixed-pattern column stripes, cycled at 30 fps), heat shimmer above hot sources.

palette.name: Absolute cold
palette.role: Ramp 0.00 – deepest shadows, overlay text outline base

palette.name: Deep cold
palette.role: Ramp 0.08 – tree canopies, hedgerows, cold puddles

palette.name: Indigo ground
palette.role: Ramp 0.18 – open soil, ground fallback colour (~45 % of the screen)

palette.name: Violet
palette.role: Ramp 0.28 – warmer soil, stubble fields, cold metal

palette.name: Purple
palette.role: Ramp 0.38 – road asphalt, dry-stone walls, rocks with stored warmth

palette.name: Magenta
palette.role: Ramp 0.48 – halos, insulated clothing edges, warm metal

palette.name: Crimson
palette.role: Ramp 0.57 – cool rims of warm bodies, cooling particles

palette.name: Red-orange
palette.role: Ramp 0.65 – outer body zones; also REC dot and hot-spot marker

palette.name: Amber
palette.role: Ramp 0.81 – warm cores, flanges, card hover

palette.name: Yellow
palette.role: Ramp 0.88 – hot cores, eyes; UI accent labels

palette.name: White-hot
palette.role: Ramp 1.00 – faces, furnace cores, flame centres, impact flash

palette.name: Camera white
palette.role: All overlay lines, brackets, readouts and HUD borders

paletteRules: Every visible colour of the scene comes from ONE ramp lookup. Never pick a colour directly for a subject – pick its temperature.
Temperature budget: water and canopies 0.03–0.14, open ground 0.12–0.30, roads/walls/rocks 0.30–0.46, warm metal and halos 0.45–0.65, bodies 0.50–0.85, faces/eyes/cores/flames 0.90–1.00.
Ground never goes above ~0.46 (purple-magenta) so every warm subject outshines it; creatures stay below ~0.9 through their bake gain and only the main character face reaches white-hot.
Each subject pairs a hot focal point with a cool part: white face + cold backpack, white eye + cool quills, white core + cool fur.
The UI is the only thing outside the ramp: camera white #eef3ff lines and text with a dark #020008 outline, plus the ramp itself as gradients in bars.
No greens, no cyans, no greys inside the image – a cyan or green pixel breaks the illusion immediately.

typography.role: All readouts: °C values, timer, counters, bar labels, timestamps, card text, floating digits
typography.css: font: 400 16px 'Share Tech Mono', monospace; color: #eef3ff; letter-spacing: 1px; text-shadow: 0 0 2px #000, 0 1px 3px #000;

typography.role: Big panel titles (ramp-gradient text) and tiny spaced labels
typography.css: font: 900 50px/1 'Orbitron', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; background: linear-gradient(180deg,#fffdf2 8%,#ffe777 30%,#fb9d12 52%,#e3443a 72%,#96158a 96%); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent;
font: 600 18px 'Chakra Petch', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1.5px; color: #fffdf2;

world.summary: A night-time patchwork landscape seen from above as a temperature field: Worley field cells (meadow, ploughed furrows, warm dry stubble, cold wet fields) separated by cold hedgerows or warm dry-stone walls, gently curving warm roads with cold gravel shoulders, flat cold ponds, faint buried heating pipes with warm manholes, and stamped residual-heat decals (boot-print trails, animal tracks, resting spots, compost heaps). Cells are ~380 units across, so a screen shows 2–4 fields and usually a road.
layers: Raw fields on a 4-unit grid: base temperature 0.19 ± 0.09 (fbm 340 u) ± 0.03 (fbm 64 u), damp hollows −0.05; Worley cell (380 u, slightly domain-warped) gives type, furrow direction and the border distance f2−f1; road distance to sinusoidal centrelines (rows every 1300 u, columns every 1500 u); water level fbm 600 u; wall-ness fbm 520 u.

Per pixel (bilinear grid + crisp thresholds): cell offsets meadow 0 / ploughed +0.018 with furrows ±0.05 every 6.5 u / stubble +0.075 / wet −0.06; tileable fine noise ±0.034 (128 u) and ±0.017 (32 u).
Field borders: hedgerow 0.10 with bumpy noise where f2−f1 < 0.034 (≈ 13 u wide), or dry-stone wall: warm core 0.34 (f2−f1 < 0.011) with cold flanks 0.125.
Roads: asphalt 0.345 within 10 u of the centreline, two slightly warmer wheel tracks (+0.03) at 5.2 u, cold gravel shoulders 0.2 out to 14 u.
Water: flat 0.10 with tiny ripples (±0.007), damp shore band −0.04, a faint warmer waterline +0.045.
Buried pipes: axis-aligned lines on a 760-unit grid, +0.07 core (σ ≈ 2.6 u) and +0.03 wide glow, warm manhole discs at their ends.

Decals (stamped into the temperature buffer before mapping): warm pebbles +0.04–0.075, cold plant clumps −0.03…−0.05, boot-print trails (1.15 × 2.05 u ovals every 6.6 u, older = cooler, +0.045…+0.13), paired animal tracks, warm resting spots 6–10 u (+0.07–0.11), compost heaps up to +0.39 in stubble fields, cold puddles in wet fields.
Mapping: temperature → 72-band ironbow LUT → ImageData, one chunk of 256 units at a time.

characters.summary: Characters are heat signatures. The main character is a small explorer in a hooded insulated parka (~14 u wide, ~30 u tall): white-hot face (1.0) inside an orange fur ruff, warm chest (0.8), cooler sleeves and legs, and a cold dark backpack (0.27) that is the darkest shape of the figure and shows the facing. Creatures: a small quilled ground critter (~27 × 17 u) with a hot chest and white eye under a cooler quill ridge; a fast flickering wisp of hot gas (~12 × 24 u, hovering) with two cold eye holes; and a large hulking knuckle-walker (~42 × 50 u) with a white-hot furnace core and glowing fissures in its chest, cooler fur on the shoulders and warm fists on the ground.
rules: Paint every part as a single temperature or a radial gradient from a warm core to a cooler edge; never choose colours.

One hot focal point per subject (face, eye, core, flame centre) and one clearly cooler part (backpack, quills, fur, eye holes) – that pairing is what makes small subjects readable; the main character owns the only white-hot point.
Silhouette first: upright figure vs. horizontal four-legged critter vs. vertical flame vs. wide frontal hulk – types differ in shape, not hue.
Bake with the shared heat pipeline: 0.55 u diffusion, limb cooling (rims up to 42 % cooler) and a 1.3–2.1 u halo for warm subjects only; this is what separates bodies in crowds.
Far limbs are 0.06–0.08 cooler than near limbs; insulated clothing is cooler than skin; noses, tail tips and feet are the coldest parts of a body.
Facing is a mirrored copy of the bake; flash, cooled-down and afterimage versions are re-mappings of the same temperature map.
Draw characters with normal source-over blending; only the baked halo provides glow, so a crowd of 60 stays readable instead of washing out.

Heat ranking: only the main character reaches white-hot (gain 1.0, halo 0.72); creatures are baked through a gain that keeps them in lower bands – critter ×0.92, hulk ×0.9, wisp ×0.86 – so the face of the main character is always the hottest pixel on screen.

props.summary: Props are cold shapes with residual warmth, baked through the same pipeline: pine trees as near-black canopies (0.03–0.14, colder than the ground) over a warm ground pool, bare dead trees, rocks that hold the day's warmth (0.46 → 0.27) – one with a warm handprint –, fence posts with a warm bird on one, an ember pit with flickering coals, and an industrial set near buried pipes: hot steam pipe runs on trestles with cooler insulated sleeves and white-hot flanges, exhaust vents with rising warm plumes, and a transformer box with cooling fins and one overheating connector.
rules: Most props are colder than the characters and many are colder than the ground: cold props read as dark silhouettes, warm props as purple-to-orange shapes.
Every prop bakes its own soft contact pool into the sprite (an ellipse at 0.25–0.42 temperature, alpha 0.4–0.85) so it sits in the ground even on a foreign floor.
Tell small stories with residual heat: a handprint on a rock, a bird on a post, an overheating connector, warm ground under trees.
Hot props get life at runtime: ember pits cross-fade between 3 baked frames and throw small rising sparks, vents and pipe valves emit cooling plume puffs, and all of them register heat shimmer.
Placement follows the world: trees line the hedgerows, rocks and ember pits sit in dry stubble fields, industrial props cluster within 48 units of a buried pipe, nothing sits on roads or water.

effects.name: Hot-streak projectile
effects.how: A white-hot head (r 2.3, 1.0 → 0.9, strong halo) in front of a 26-unit wedge-shaped trail painted as a temperature gradient 0.4 → 0.97 with alpha 0 → 1; the trail grows from 15 % to full length in its first 0.1 s and fades in its last 0.15 s.

effects.name: Heat burst
effects.how: On dissolve: an instant white-hot puff (radius 1.25–1.5 × body radius, 0.2 s), 5–10 rising puffs that grow 1.8x and cool from 0.98 down the ramp over 0.6–1.05 s, 9–18 ember streaks with gravity that cool from 1.0 to 0.45, and a shock ring 0.6r → 3.4r (5r large) at temperature 1.0 → 0.58.

effects.name: Residual heat imprint
effects.how: A flat soft ellipse where the body was (0.42 height ratio), temperature 0.5–0.62 cooling to half, fading over 2.6 s (4 s for the large creature); drawn under the actors.

effects.name: Impact flash
effects.how: The struck body is redrawn with the flash transfer t + (1 − t) × 0.86 (white-hot) at alpha = flash, plus 4 short hot sparks and a small white puff.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a pulsing ember shard (diamond 6 × 9.6 u, core 0.8–0.93 over 6 frames at 5 fps). Large: a hot hexagonal cell (r 5.2, core 0.9–1.0, cooler inner ring). Both float ±0.8 u above a warm puff and leave two cooled afterimages while flying.

effects.name: Orbiting heat orb
effects.how: A white-hot orb (r 3.4) with a tilted cooler ring, pulsing ±6 %, trailing a 14-sample arc of residual heat whose segments cool from 0.9 to 0.45 and thin from 3.2 to 0.8 units.

effects.name: Breath and footprints
effects.how: The main character exhales warm clouds (0.62 → 0.32, growing 1.4 → 5 u) every 2.4 s and leaves warm footprints every 6.5 units that cool from 0.48 to 0.24 over 5 s; the large creature leaves big prints every 12 units for 7 s.

effects.name: Spawn and dissolve
effects.how: Spawning creatures appear as a cold silhouette (transfer 0.1 + 0.34 t) that warms up to full heat while a shrinking ring closes in; dissolving creatures cross-fade to the cold version while slumping (width +16 %, height −38 %).

atmosphere.summary: The camera is the atmosphere: no light, no shadows – warm contact glows under bodies, a lens vignette that cools the frame edges, animated sensor grain with fixed-pattern column stripes, heat shimmer above hot sources, an auto-gain flash on strong heat events, and a full camera overlay: corner brackets, a centre reticle with a spot-meter readout, a vertical temperature scale bar, REC timer, timestamp, a NUC indicator and an auto-tracking box with a °C label on the hottest large subject.
rules: Contact glow instead of shadows: a radial sprite from ramp 0.44 at 80 % via 0.37 at 42 % to 0, as a flat ellipse 0.42 high; radius 12 u under the main character, creature radius × 1.45 (wisp × 1.9 at 55 %, large × 1.6).
Vignette: radial from 34 % of the short side to 56 % of the diagonal, rgba(3,1,12,0) → rgba(3,1,12,.24) at 62 % → rgba(2,0,7,.72).

Grain: 4 pre-baked 160 px tiles of light (alpha ≤ 15·|n|) and dark (alpha ≤ 36·|n|) speckles with column stripes ±0.12 and row offsets ±0.06, cycled 30 times per second at a random offset, plain source-over – never a full-screen blend mode.
Heat shimmer: regions above hot sources are copied once and redrawn in 0.9-unit strips shifted sideways by sin(y·0.9 − t·8) × 0.35–0.7 units, strongest in the lower middle of the region.
Auto gain: strong heat events add a 'screen' wash of #fdc52e at up to 32 % that decays with exp(−5t).

Overlay geometry (u = screen height / 900): brackets 58u long at a 30u margin, 2.2u lines over a 4.2u dark under-stroke; reticle ticks at 63–81u around the subject; scale bar 13u × 36 % of the height with 5 labelled ticks 48.6 … −12.4 °C.

Tracking box: four corner brackets around the hottest large subject near the centre, 0.7 u camera-white over a 1.5 u dark stroke, shrinking from 1.7x to 1x within 0.25 s when it acquires a new subject, then a red hot-spot triangle and a °C label.

ui.summary: The HUD is the camera's own UI: thin camera-white 1 px borders on near-black translucent panels, square corners, bars filled with the ironbow ramp itself and divided into 10 % segments, tick marks under the top bar, bracket-framed timer, Share Tech Mono readouts with a dark text outline, Orbitron titles with ramp-gradient text, and cards framed by corner brackets with a thermal-image icon in an inset viewport and a ramp stripe at the bottom.

motion: Main character walk: 8 baked poses, legs swing ±3.8 u with a 1.9 u foot lift, the body lowest just after each contact (0.9·sin(2a − 2.33)), the hood landing late (+0.35 u), arms swinging 0.8 rad against the legs; idle: 8 poses over 3.4 s – breathing, forearms hugged in front against the cold with small shivers and a foot stamp at 56 % of the cycle; dash: launch crouch (0.3 rad) → streak (stretch 15 %) → brake with a landing squash, 4 cooled afterimages whose spacing grows with the dash; hurt: recoil pose with a gasping mouth.
Small critter: 8 frames, four legs alternating ±1.9 u, body bob 0.8 u, tail sway; frame = anim × 0.4.

Wisp: 8 flicker frames played at 8–13 fps per actor (flame tongues travel up the edge), hot gas rises quickly and sinks slowly (eased hover 2.2–5.4 u), alpha flicker 80–100 % at 24 Hz, two cooled afterimages at −0.06 s and −0.12 s of velocity.
Large hulk: 8 frames, bob 1.3 u, arms swing alternately with fists lifting 2.8 u (knuckle walk), a cooling ring 14 → 30 u on each footfall, big warm footprints.
Hot props: ember pits cross-fade between 3 frames at 2.4 Hz; vent plumes rise 30 u in 2.4 s while growing to 10 u and cooling from 0.8 to 0.38.

Temperature is the animation channel: things appear by rising from a crouch (scale 0.7 → 1 with a 7 % overshoot) while the cold silhouette warms through a mid-warm stage to full heat; they vanish with a white-hot flare and recoil (first 18 %) after which the heat drains hot → warm → cold while the body slumps into a puddle (46 % lower, 22 % wider) and a heat imprint stays on the ground; hits flash white-hot with a damped squash (15 %, ~250 ms) and a knock-back push; particles always cool as they age.
Camera: REC dot blinks at 0.8 Hz, the spot meter jitters ±0.2 °C twice a second, the NUC label blinks every 16 s, the tracking box snaps in within 0.25 s.
do: Paint gray temperatures and map them through one ramp – for sprites, ground, particles and icons alike.
Give every subject one white-hot focal point and one clearly cold part.
Bake rim cooling and hot-only halos once; draw sprites with plain drawImage at runtime.
Keep the ground in the indigo–purple band (≤ 0.46) and the props mostly colder than the characters.
Tell stories with residual heat: footprints, handprints, imprints of dissolved bodies, warm ground under trees.
Let particles cool through the ramp as they age (white → yellow → orange → crimson → gone).
Frame the image with the camera UI: brackets, scale bar, °C readouts, REC, grain, vignette.
dont: Don't pick colours per subject – a single off-ramp colour (green, cyan, grey) breaks the illusion.
Don't draw outlines; separate bodies with temperature contrast, rim cooling and halos.
Don't make the ground warm or busy – above ~0.46 it competes with the bodies.
Don't make everything hot: without cold parts and cold props the image turns into an orange soup.
Don't use additive blending for bodies or shadowBlur/ctx.filter at runtime.
Don't run a per-pixel colour pass over the full screen each frame – map temperatures once at bake time.
Don't use soft rounded fonts or coloured panels; the UI is a measuring instrument.
performance: Baked once in init (~0.4 s): main character 8 walk + 8 idle + 3 dash + 1 recoil, small critter 8, wisp 8, large hulk 8 frames, each through the JS heat pipeline (4 box blurs per sprite) with normal/flash/cold/afterimage/warm variants and mirrored copies; collectibles 2 × 6 pulse frames, projectile head + trail, orb, 9 prop sprites, 16 puff sprites, grain tiles. Ground: chunk generator with ~80 short steps (grid rows, pixel rows, decal passes), 25–40 ms per 256-unit chunk, noise from periodic pixel tables, per-cell feature flags so open field skips the edge math. Per frame: one drawImage per sprite (2–3 for afterimages), particles as single strokes or puff blits, one grain pattern fill, up to 10 small strip copies for heat shimmer, one cached overlay image and a handful of cached text bitmaps. Measured against the previous version in the same session (heavily loaded machine): play frame x0.70, chunk build x0.80, dense stage x0.93 – i.e. no measurable extra cost; the new poses and variants only add bake time at init.
